ambiguities.aspect: previous-input register update while reset is high
readings: The previous-input register is held at its reset value while reset is high, so a 1->0 transition that spans reset is not detected.
The previous-input register continues to sample in on every rising edge even when reset is high, so a bit that is 1 during reset and 0 after reset sets out.

ambiguities.aspect: reset value of the previous-input register
readings: Reset forces the previous-input register to 0, so after reset the first 0 sample cannot set out.
Reset does not affect the previous-input register (or initializes it to 1/unknown), so a 0 after reset can set out immediately if the pre-reset or initial value was 1.

ambiguities.aspect: priority between reset and falling-edge capture on the same rising edge
readings: Reset dominates: if reset=1, out clears to 0 and any simultaneous 1->0 transition is ignored.
Capture dominates: if a bit falls on the same edge that reset=1, out[bit] is set to 1 and remains 1 until a later reset.

ambiguities.aspect: output latency from the sampled 0 to out=1
readings: out[bit] updates to 1 on the same rising edge that samples in[bit]=0 after it was previously 1; the new value is visible immediately after that edge.
out[bit] updates to 1 one rising edge later than the edge that samples the 0, as if the falling-edge detect is registered before setting out.
